abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) isolates servers by design: only the host can orchestrate cross-server workflows. When the host is a large language model, the resulting orchestrations are non-deterministic, non-reproducible, and pay one inference round-trip per tool call. We present a coordination architecture in which a Hierarchical Task Network (HTN) planner generates a verifiable cross-server plan once, and a runtime middleware executes it deterministically across multiple MCP servers, binding cross-action data dependencies via a template mechanism (\verb|${context.X}|) substituted at execution time. The architecture mirrors MCP's isolation constraint: each compound task decomposes into server-local primitive actions, and inter-server data flow is bound at execution time via JSON-path output extractors. We instantiate the architecture on five HTN domains spanning laboratory robotics, bioinformatics and multiscale modelling, and demonstrate end-to-end execution from a browser-based plan controller against eight live third-party MCP servers querying real biological databases.
